name: ThirdDraft: AI Blog Writer & SEO Autopilot
author: ThirdDraft

sections.description:
ThirdDraft writes SEO blog articles for your business and publishes them to WordPress. Every article arrives researched, reviewed and ready to go live, with its pictures, its sources and your SEO plugin’s fields filled in.

Connect once, and finished articles appear as native posts on the days you planned. Publish them straight away, or keep them as drafts to read first.

What you get

  • Articles built around your business. ThirdDraft reads your website and plans topics from the searches your customers really make.
  • Facts you can check. Every article comes with the sources it was researched from.
  • A calendar you control. Move articles between days as your priorities change.
  • Native WordPress posts. Headings, lists, tables and pictures arrive as blocks you edit like any other post. Sites on the classic editor get classic content.
  • Pictures in your Media Library. Every picture is copied in with its alt text, and the first one becomes the featured image.
  • Your SEO plugin, filled in. The title, description and focus keyword go into Yoast SEO, Rank Math, All in One SEO, SEOPress or The SEO Framework. Values you set yourself stay as you set them.
  • Published or saved as a draft. You choose, for each site.
  • Found by search engines sooner. Each new post is announced to Bing and the other IndexNow search engines as soon as it goes live.

How it works

  1. Install and activate the plugin.
  2. In Settings → ThirdDraft, click Connect to ThirdDraft and confirm in ThirdDraft.
  3. Choose Publish or Save as draft.
  4. Articles arrive as they are finished, each on its day.

What you need

  • A ThirdDraft account with this site added to it. Your first article is free.
  • WordPress 5.6 or later, PHP 7.2 or later, and HTTPS on your site.

External services

This plugin connects your site to ThirdDraft, the service that writes your articles. It talks to ThirdDraft only for the following:

  • Connecting. When you click Connect, your browser goes to ThirdDraft with your site’s address, the address articles are sent to, the plugin and WordPress versions, and one-time values that secure the connection. Your site then fetches the connection’s secret from ThirdDraft directly.
  • Receiving articles. ThirdDraft sends each finished article, signed with that secret, to your site. The plugin downloads the article’s pictures from ThirdDraft. Its answers tell ThirdDraft each post’s id, address, status and when it was last edited, and the plugin’s version; ThirdDraft can also ask, signed the same way, how a post it sent stands, and the plugin answers with the same.
  • Try again and Disconnect. When you click either, your site sends ThirdDraft the connection’s id, signed with the secret.
  • Checks. When you open Settings → ThirdDraft, your site makes one request to ThirdDraft to check that it can reach it.

The plugin’s requests to ThirdDraft carry your site’s address in their user agent.

ThirdDraft’s Terms of service and Privacy policy.

When a post from ThirdDraft is published, the plugin also sends IndexNow the post’s address, your site’s host and your site’s IndexNow key, which it shares with the search engines that take part. The key is published at your site’s address as a text file, so they can check it. You can switch this off in Settings → ThirdDraft. See IndexNow’s terms.
sections.installation:
1. In WordPress, go to Plugins → Add New, search for “ThirdDraft” and click Install Now.
  2. Click Activate. WordPress opens Settings → ThirdDraft.
  3. Click Connect to ThirdDraft, sign in to ThirdDraft if asked, choose Publish or Save as draft, and click Connect.

The page says Connected once ThirdDraft has reached your site. Articles arrive as they are finished.

You can also download the plugin from your ThirdDraft account, or as a zip file, and install it from Plugins → Add New → Upload Plugin.
sections.faq:
Is ThirdDraft an AI writer or an autoblogging plugin?

ThirdDraft is an AI writer: it researches each topic, writes the article, has it reviewed and revised, and adds its pictures. With this plugin it is also blog automation: each finished article becomes a post on your site, published on its day or saved as a draft, as you choose. You can also have ThirdDraft wait for you to approve each article before it is sent.

Do I need a ThirdDraft account?

Yes. The plugin receives articles from ThirdDraft and does nothing on its own. ThirdDraft is a subscription per website, and your first article is free.

Does the plugin send visitor data?

No. The plugin adds no scripts or tracking to your site’s pages, sets no cookies and sends nothing about your visitors anywhere. What it does send, and when, is listed under External services.

How are duplicate posts prevented?

An article sent again updates its post instead of making a new one, and pictures already in your Media Library are reused.

Where do I choose between publishing and saving drafts?

In ThirdDraft, when you connect, and later in ThirdDraft’s Publishing settings for your site.

Can I edit a post after it arrives?

Yes. It is an ordinary WordPress post. If ThirdDraft sends a newer version of the same article, the post’s text is updated and your earlier text stays in its revisions. Search titles, descriptions and keywords you changed yourself are kept.

What happens to a published post when its article is updated?

It stays published, at the same address and with the same date.

Can ThirdDraft change a post I edited?

No. ThirdDraft only adds a link to a newer article, and only in a post that nobody has edited since ThirdDraft sent it. Posts you edited, unpublished or deleted are left as they are.

I deleted a post by mistake.

Restore it from the trash, or send the article again from ThirdDraft: a post in the trash counts as gone, and a new one is made.

The page says ThirdDraft couldn’t reach this site.

The page lists what to fix. Most often a security plugin or firewall blocks requests to the address articles arrive at; allow requests to the address shown on the page. Then click Try again.

The page says the site’s clock is off.

ThirdDraft’s requests are valid for five minutes. Ask your host to correct the server’s time.

Which search engines hear of a new post?

Those that take part in IndexNow, such as Bing, Yandex, Naver, Seznam and Yep. Google does not take part. Each post’s address is sent once, when the post is published, and again if its address changes. Nothing is sent from a site whose WordPress environment type is not production, such as a staging copy, or while the site asks search engines not to index it (Settings → Reading). Switch it off in Settings → ThirdDraft.

Does the plugin work on multisite?

Yes. Each site connects on its own, from its own Settings → ThirdDraft.

How do updates arrive?

From WordPress.org, like any other plugin: on the Plugins and Updates screens, where you can also switch automatic updates on or off.

What happens if I deactivate or delete the plugin?

Deactivating keeps the connection and settings, but ThirdDraft can’t deliver while the plugin is inactive. When you activate it again, the plugin asks ThirdDraft to check the connection, and the articles that waited arrive. Deleting the plugin removes its settings and connection. Your posts and pictures stay, so installing the plugin again updates them rather than making copies.
sections.changelog:
1.3.0

  • A picture’s title in the Media Library, taken from its alt text, ends at a whole word.
  • Updates now come from WordPress.org, like any other plugin’s.

1.2.0

  • ThirdDraft can add a link to a newer article in a post it sent earlier, without anybody asking. The plugin takes such a change only while the post is published and nobody has edited it since ThirdDraft last wrote it: it never overwrites your edits, never publishes a post and never makes a new one.
  • Each answer to ThirdDraft says the post’s status, when it was last edited and the plugin’s version.

1.1.0

  • Bing and the other search engines that take part in IndexNow are told of each post from ThirdDraft as soon as it is published, and again when its address changes. On by default; switch it off in Settings → ThirdDraft.

1.0.0

  • First release: connect with one click; articles as native posts with their pictures, search title, description and focus keyword; publish or save as draft; automatic updates.
